- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +1.0 sentiment) by overshooting — cap forecast peaks at 1–2% above recent high.
- In 30-day horizon, model shows persistent lag in capturing true trend — add 0.5–1.0 to forecast if recent 5-day average is rising.
- If sentiment history shows no clear direction (all 0.00), model tends to be flat; apply slight upward bias if price has been consolidating.
- Avoid overfitting to recent 1–2 day highs — if forecast exceeds 3 consecutive days above true, reduce by 1–2% to prevent overcorrection.
- In low-sentiment periods, model underestimates mean reversion — add 0.5–1.0 to forecast if true outcome is trending upward from 3–5 days ago.
